gap: No result ChatGPT got states, side by side and read on one day, what each 40,000 mAh-plus bank with a 140 W USB-C port costs and whether it can be bought: on 2026-11-26 UGREEN's 48,000 mAh (153.6 Wh) is $118.99 in stock at us.ugreen.com, AOHi's Starship 40K is $179.00 in stock at iaohi.com, and the Cuktech 30 that ChatGPT picked first is unavailable at cuktech.com behind a $999.00 placeholder price.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's MacBook power bank roundup (first 100,000 of 140,322 characters read) and powerbanks.fyi's laptop list; Tom's Guide, the other cited page, returned only navigation text and could not be compared. Macworld already has part of it: the UGREEN 48,000 mAh at '$118.99 at Amazon' today, 153.6 Wh, 3.6 lb, and 1.8 charges of a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro. In the part read it lists no other bank over 100 Wh, so no AOHi 40K and no Cuktech 30. powerbanks.fyi lists only two banks at this size, shows the UGREEN at a stale $169.99 ('Checked on Aug 18', no year) and the Cuktech 30 as 'Price unavailable (sold out)', and has no AOHi 40K. Neither page prices the whole size class on one date, gives a price per watt-hour, or explains why ChatGPT quoted the AOHi at $259.99 in one chat and $179.00 in the other.
decides: It removes ChatGPT's first pick and reorders the rest. The Cuktech 30 cannot be bought from its maker's store today, and the Amazon search for it returned nothing. Of the two 140 W banks that can be bought, the UGREEN gives 8,000 mAh more for $60.01 less than the AOHi's store price, or $24.21 less than the AOHi's $143.20 code price. That is about $0.77 per Wh against $0.98 (code) or $1.23 (store). So the UGREEN 48,000 mAh wins on capacity and price; it is a partner-store product with no record yet. The AOHi Starship 40K (our record) keeps the exact-40,000 mAh, soda-can-size segment (2.09 × 2.56 × 6.77 in), but its weight advantage was not sourced today. The Techsmarter 100 W bank could not be priced or specified from any page that opened, so it cannot be ranked on this evidence.
